summary: Security audit of Quick Play matchmaking implementation. No vulnerabilities found. Auth correctly reuses apiFetch Bearer token pattern with no new auth paths. categorySlug is hardcoded ('tech'), not user-derived — no injection risk. duelId from server response used only for client-side react-router navigation, not outbound URLs. Cleanup on unmount properly leaves queue via best-effort DELETE. 429 handled without automatic retry (no retry storms). stopPolling() called before startPolling() in every path prevents interval accumulation. No new trust boundaries, no secrets in client code, no user-derived URL construction.
goal: Security audit of 1v1 Quick Play implementation

learnings.insight: duelId from server poll response is used without format validation (e.g., UUID check) before navigation. Acceptable since react-router treats it as an in-app path segment and the server is the trusted source, but explicit validation would be defense-in-depth.
learnings.action: No action required. If adding format validation in the future, validate as UUID before navigate().
